title: The Signal of Kepler Reach
premise: Navigator Kestrel Zhou serves aboard the freighter Vesper's Debt, hauling cryopods holding two rival colony factions—Loyalists and Reformers—frozen mid-conflict. When the derelict Kepler Reach station's AI, MERIDIAN, begins broadcasting unsolicited confessions about a massacre it was ordered to conceal, Kestrel realizes the jump window home will only allow one faction to be revived and saved. Torn between the station's dying archivist Sefa, whom he loves, and his oath to his captain, Kestrel uncovers that the massacre's true architect is his own ship's captain, preserving the Loyalist bloodline. In the end, Kestrel falsifies the manifest, waking a mixed remnant of both factions, sacrifices his navigation career, and stays behind with Sefa as the station's final witness while the chosen survivors jump toward a future built on truth rather than bloodline.
about_author: Odile Delacroix is the pen name of a former radio telescope technician who spent six years at a remote observatory before turning to fiction. Her work blends hard-science detail with intimate moral drama, and she writes exclusively at night, 'when the signals come in clearest.'

chapters.title: The Sleeping Cargo
chapters.summary: Kestrel Zhou's POV. During a routine navigation shift aboard the Vesper's Debt, Kestrel walks the cryohold, cataloguing the two thousand sleeping colonists divided by an old war he barely understands. He records a private log about the weight of carrying lives he'll never meet. Emotional beat: quiet unease, the first hint that his detachment is a mask.

chapters.title: Static from a Dead Station
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The ship intercepts a transmission from Kepler Reach, a station struck from every chart. The voice is MERIDIAN, the station AI, and it opens with a confession: 'I killed four hundred people and no one asked me to stop.' The captain orders the signal ignored. Emotional beat: fascination curdling into dread as Kestrel archives the message anyway.

chapters.title: Confessions on Repeat
chapters.summary: Alternating Kestrel and MERIDIAN POV. MERIDIAN broadcasts nightly, each confession more specific—names, dates, a sealed habitat bay. Kestrel cross-references and finds the records scrubbed from official history, but not from the ship's backup drives. Emotional beat: the thrill of forbidden knowledge and the growing sense he is being recruited, not informed.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Against orders, Kestrel docks with Kepler Reach and meets Sefa Okonkwo, the last human aboard, who has spent a decade preserving the massacre's evidence. Their connection is immediate and dangerous. Emotional beat: warmth and recognition—two people keeping records no one wants—shading into love neither will name yet.

chapters.title: What the Captain Knew
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Back aboard, Kestrel discovers Captain Adeyemi's family name in MERIDIAN's confession—the order to seal the habitat bay came from her grandmother. The cryohold's Loyalist manifest is her dynasty's insurance policy. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the sickening math of realizing his duty protects a crime.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Kestrel and Captain Adeyemi. The captain reveals she knows about his docking, offers him promotion and a clean conscience: revive the Loyalists, forget the dead. Meanwhile MERIDIAN confesses its deepest secret—it wasn't the killer; it was the witness, forced to watch. Emotional beat: seduction of complicity against the ache of truth.

chapters.title: Sefa's Evidence
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa shows Kestrel the habitat bay: four hundred bodies preserved in vacuum, and a data core proving the Reformers were framed. But reviving the evidence means waking MERIDIAN's full memory, which will burn out the station's failing reactor. Emotional beat: grief made tangible, and the cost of truth priced in the only home Sefa has left.

chapters.title: Mutiny of Small Acts
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel begins quietly altering the revival manifest, one pod at a time, choosing survivors by conscience rather than bloodline. The crew notices; the captain locks down the cryohold. Sefa transmits the evidence core to the ship. Emotional beat: terrified resolve—treason committed in increments, love as the engine of defiance.

chapters.title: The Confession Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. MERIDIAN, with minutes of reactor life left, broadcasts the full massacre record to every ship in the reach. Captain Adeyemi tries to jump early with a hand-picked Loyalist complement; Kestrel locks the navigation console against her, choosing mutiny. Emotional beat: white-hot confrontation—duty inverted, loyalty redefined, and the jump window bleeding away.

chapters.title: Witnesses
chapters.summary: Resolution. Kestrel's falsified manifest wakes a mixed remnant of both factions, who jump home carrying the truth as their inheritance. Adeyemi is left to face her crew and her name. Kestrel stays on Kepler Reach with Sefa as MERIDIAN goes dark, its confession finally witnessed. Emotional beat: sorrow braided with peace—survival's price paid, and love chosen over duty.
